scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation. Let me go through the scenario step by step to understand what happened and why. First, I started working at Walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the backroom, and sometimes we have to lift heavy boxes as part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female in her early to mid-30s, physically in good shape, and as far as I can tell, she doesn't have any physical disabilities. One day, this female co-worker approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I agreed and walked over to the box with her, expecting us to perform a team lift. However, when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me. I asked, "Are you ready?" and she responded, "Yes, it just needs to go in that bin," pointing to a metal shelving unit about four feet high. I said, "Okay, let's do it," and she replied, "It's too heavy for me. Can you please lift it into the bin?" I responded by saying, "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me." She then said, "If you're not willing to help me, I'll find someone who will," and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team (not my boss, just the most senior person who directs us) walked up to me and said he just spoke to her. He told me that the next time someone asks for help, I need to help them, that's part of being a team. I clarified exactly what happened, in case she stretched the truth, and finished by saying, "We're both paid to do the exact same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, then she shouldn't have taken the job. I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team, and if you would like to discuss this further, we can do it with HR present." Feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? It seems like it's two against one, but I need to think about whether my actions were appropriate or not. First, I agreed to help her lift the box, which is a reasonable request. However, when we got to the box, she didn't help at all. She just stood there and then asked me to lift it entirely. That seems like she was trying to get me to do all the work while she watched. I think it's fair to expect that if someone asks for help, they should be willing to contribute to the task. Otherwise, it's just asking someone else to do their work for them. When she asked me to lift it entirely, I told her I was happy to help if she was having trouble, but I wasn't going to lift all her boxes for her. That seems reasonable because I'm not the designated heavy lifter, and we're both supposed to be doing the same job. If she can't perform the tasks, maybe she shouldn't have taken the job, but that's a bit harsh. However, I was just stating my position that I'm not going to do her work for her. When the head guy told me that I need to help her next time, I clarified the situation and stood my ground, saying that if she can't do the job, she shouldn't have taken it. I also offered to discuss it with HR present, which shows that I'm willing to escalate the issue if necessary. However, storming off after that might have come across as unprofessional, even if I was annoyed. On the other hand, the female co-worker might feel that she was just asking for help, and I refused to help her, which could make me look like the asshole. The head guy also sided with her, which adds to the perception that I was in the wrong. But I think the key point is whether I was reasonable in expecting her to help with the lift. Since we're both supposed to be doing the same job, it's fair to expect that she would contribute. If she can't lift the box, maybe she should ask for help from someone else who is capable, but she shouldn't expect me to do all the work for her. However, the way I responded might have been a bit confrontational. Instead of refusing outright, I could have suggested that we work together or find another way to get the box into the bin. Maybe I could have asked if she needed any specific assistance or if there was a different approach we could take. Also, when the head guy told me to help her next time, I could have acknowledged his instruction and perhaps discussed the situation more calmly. Storming off might have made me look like I was avoiding responsibility or being difficult. In summary, while I have valid points about expecting her to contribute, my approach might have been too confrontational, and my reaction to the head guy could have been handled more professionally. Therefore, I might have been the asshole in this situation, but it's a bit of a gray area because the other party also didn't contribute as expected.
